question: Why are West & South claims taking longer to close since May 2026?

report.interpretation: Cycle time is the agreed metric: median days from report date to close date, for closed claims, grouped by report month. The region is West & South (WA and SA), motor and home combined. I compared January to April 2026 with May to July 2026. I left out August and September because most of those claims are still open, so their cycle time looks artificially short.
report.answer: The slowdown is real, and the data points to lost adjuster capacity. The median time to close West & South claims was about 22 to 30 days from January to April. It rose to 40 days for claims reported in May, 44 in June and 40.5 in July. NSW & ACT, the comparison region I checked, did not slow down: its median stayed at 24 to 29 days. Two of the six West & South adjusters left: ADJ-025 on 1 May and ADJ-026 on 15 May. Neither has been assigned claims since (ADJ-025 last on 14 April, ADJ-026 had one on 4 May). The four remaining adjusters (ADJ-027 to ADJ-030) took over the work. They each received about 100 claims reported from May to September, against about 40 in January to April. Each of the four remaining adjusters now has a median close time of 38 to 45 days, up from 25 to 29. The slowdown shows in every cause of loss and in both WA and SA, which fits a capacity shortage better than a problem with one type of claim, one state or one person. Reported volume also rose a little. West & South averaged about 76 claims a month from May to July, against about 60 from January to April. That is a smaller rise than the loss of 2 of 6 adjusters, and I did not test volume as a separate cause. This is correlation in the data, not proof of cause. I did not check the reasons for the departures or any handover arrangements.
report.answer_sql: select date_trunc('month',report_date) as rep_month, count(*) as claims, median(close_date-report_date) filter(where status='closed') as median_days_to_close, count(distinct adjuster_id) as adjusters from claims where region='West & South' and report_date between '2026-01-01' and '2026-07-31' group by 1 order by 1

findings.claim: The median days to close West & South claims jumped from May 2026, from 22 to 30 days to 40 to 44 days. The number of adjusters handling new claims fell from 6 to 4.
findings.evidence_sql: select date_trunc('month',report_date) as rep_month, count(*) as claims, median(close_date-report_date) filter(where status='closed') as median_days_to_close, count(distinct adjuster_id) as adjusters from claims where region='West & South' and report_date between '2026-01-01' and '2026-07-31' group by 1 order by 1

findings.claim: Two West & South adjusters left in May 2026: ADJ-025 on 1 May and ADJ-026 on 15 May. The four who remain received about 100 claims each from May onward, compared with about 40 each from January to April.
findings.evidence_sql: select a.adjuster_id,a.leave_date, count(*) filter(where report_date between '2026-01-01' and '2026-04-30') pre_rep, count(*) filter(where report_date>='2026-05-01') post_rep from adjusters a left join claims c on c.adjuster_id=a.adjuster_id where a.region='West & South' group by all order by 1

hypotheses.hypothesis: Adjuster attrition and heavier caseloads for those who stayed
hypotheses.evidence: Two of six adjusters left in May. Each of the four who stayed has a median close time of 38 to 45 days, up from 25 to 29.

hypotheses.hypothesis: A change in the mix of claims (cause or product) or a problem in one state
hypotheses.evidence: Median close time rose across every cause of loss with data (for example motor collision 21 to 32 days and home water damage 31.5 to 51 days) and in both WA and SA (28 to 38 days in WA, 22 to 42.5 days in SA).
All four remaining adjusters slowed by a similar amount, from 25 to 29 days before to 38 to 45 days after.
Monthly reported claims rose from about 60 to about 76. Volume per adjuster rose far more because of the departures, and I did not separate the two effects.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Data problem (duplicate rows or incomplete months)
hypotheses.evidence: There are no duplicate claim rows. I excluded August and September, which are incomplete, from the comparison.

hypotheses.hypothesis: The slowdown is just a seasonal or normal-variation effect
hypotheses.evidence: Monthly medians from January to April were stable at 22 to 30 days, and NSW & ACT did not slow.

data_quality_issues.issue: August and September 2026 report months are mostly still open (47% and 82% open in West & South). Cycle time only counts closed claims.
data_quality_issues.impact: Those months show a falsely low cycle time (30 and 9 days), so I excluded them. The real slowdown is probably larger than the figures shown.

charts.title: West & South median days to close, by report month
charts.sql: select date_trunc('month',report_date) as rep_month, median(close_date-report_date) filter(where status='closed') as median_days_to_close from claims where region='West & South' and report_date between '2026-01-01' and '2026-07-31' group by 1 order by 1

proposed_actions.title: Review West & South adjuster capacity
proposed_actions.reason: Two adjusters left in May and have not been replaced in the data. The four remaining adjusters carry about 2.5 times their earlier intake of new claims. Consider backfilling or temporary reallocation to another region.

open_questions: Were ADJ-025 and ADJ-026 replaced, or were their open claims reassigned? Hire dates and handover records are not in the data I checked.
